The process of finding such a vector is called the composition of a vector. Following are the processes: 2.3.1 Triangle Law of Vector Addition: If two vectors can be represented by the two sides of a triangle both in magnitude and order, the third side of the triangle taken in opposite order represents the resultant. Let P⃗⃗ and Q⃗⃗⃗ be the two given vectors. Let A⃗⃗⃗⃗B⃗⃗ = P⃗⃗ and B⃗⃗⃗⃗C⃗⃗ = Q⃗⃗⃗ be the two given vectors represented by the two sides of a triangle in magnitude and direction. Then A⃗⃗⃗⃗⃗C⃗ = R⃗⃗ be the closing side of the triangle representing the resultant of the two vectors. And, one writes, R⃗⃗ =P⃗⃗+ Q⃗⃗⃗ Fig 2.4 Triangle Law of Vectors To find the magnitude and the direction of the resultant: Let's draw CD normal on AB produced where θ is the angle between the vectors.
